FLAKE-RESOLVESITE (found 2026-05-20, Phase 5 pre-flight; NOT blocking, NOT a regression): `tests/integration/resolveSite.test.ts > does not run middleware on routes mounted before it (/healthz)` rarely fails asserting /healthz==200 but receiving 403. ROOT CAUSE CLASS: root vitest project uses pool:forks + singleFork (one shared process) and mixes node + jsdom (`// @vitest-environment jsdom`) test files; some cross-file global-state leak makes a *fresh* express app's pre-middleware /healthz route return 403 (no 403 exists in src; no MSW/nock/undici/prototype-patch found — exact polluter NOT yet isolated). It is ORDER-DEPENDENT: vitest's default sequencer sorts files by cached durations, so a transient warm-cache order can place the polluter immediately before resolveSite. Self-heals as the cache converges; ~1/3 only in the transient state; never reproduced under cold cache, --reporter=verbose, integration-only, or forced/identity-sequencer order. EVIDENCE CI-SAFE: 3/3 cold-cache full runs = 297/0 (CI builds always start cold → deterministic glob order → green). RECOMMENDED FIX (dedicated cleanup task, do NOT bundle into Phase 5): either (a) split node vs jsdom into separate vitest projects so they never share a fork, or (b) drop singleFork / enable per-file isolate for the node project (watch for test-DB migrate/seed races — singleFork was likely chosen to serialize DB access), and/or add restoreMocks+unstubGlobals+unstubEnvs and hunt the leaked global. Could not verify a fix this run because the flake was not reliably reproducible after the cache self-healed.
